$comment: Tenant-isolation classification for every API module. Enforced by
scripts/check-tenant-scope.mjs in CI. A module that is not declared here
fails the build: an undeclared data path is an unreviewed one.
tenant-scoped  — owns tenant data; every read and write composes the
tenant field with the caller's filter.
global         — deliberately crosses or precedes tenant boundaries.
Requires a reason. Adding a tenant filter to one of
these is a defect, not a fix.
no-persistence — holds no repository; nothing to scope.

admin-management.reason: Super-admin surface that manages admin accounts across every tenant; scoping it would make cross-tenant administration impossible.

auth.reason: Authentication precedes tenant resolution. Credential lookup and login-attempt records are keyed by email before a tenant is known, so the tenant middleware cannot have run yet.

mail.reason: Transactional send only; owns no repository.

organizations.reason: This is the tenant registry itself. findBySlug is called by TenantMiddleware to establish tenant context, so it must resolve before any tenant scope exists.

push-notifications.reason: Dispatch service; reads through the push-tokens repository, which carries the tenant scope.

s3.reason: Presigned URL issuance; owns no repository.

scheduler-locks.reason: Cross-replica mutual-exclusion primitive. Locks are named singletons across the whole deployment; scoping them per tenant would let one lock be acquired concurrently by every tenant and break the guarantee it exists to provide.

unscopedReads.reason: Lookups are keyed by the store-issued (store, storeReference) pair, which is uniquely indexed across the collection, and every read path is a store webhook carrying no session and therefore no tenant. Ownership is enforced by the userId check in savePurchase; organizationId is persisted for reporting and is read from the record rather than supplied by a caller.

turnstile.reason: Stateless bot-protection verification against an external API.

unscopedReads.reason: Credential and identity lookups run before tenant context exists — the tenant is derived from the account these resolve.
